📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 19 Nov 2026 09:14, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 09:40.

A modern Premier League rivalry will be renewed on Saturday evening, when champions Arsenal make the long trek north to battle Newcastle United following the international break.

The Gunners entered the hiatus on the back of a fifth straight win, edging out Hull City 1-0, while Matthias Jaissle's inconsistent troops settled for a 1-1 draw at Fulham.

The Hull low block momentarily appeared capable of withstanding all of Arsenal's huffing and puffing two weekends ago, but the holders were belatedly rewarded for their endeavours when Martin Odegaard tucked home a second-half rebound.

Arsenal's task would have been easier had they been awarded a first-half penalty for Nobel Mendy's shirt pull on an offside Kai Havertz - the Premier League's Key Match Incidents panel has now ruled that the failure to award a spot kick was incorrect - but as champions do, they found a way to triumph while not at their finest.

Courtesy of their 34th 1-0 Premier League win under Mikel Arteta - the most by any coach since he took charge in December 2019 - and Manchester City's latest setback at Nottingham Forest, Arsenal opened up a five-point advantage at the top of the Premier League table before international football intervened.

Furthermore, the Gunners' total of 27 points from their opening 10 games of a Premier League season can only be bested by the 28 accrued by Chelsea in 2005-06, Manchester City in 2011-12, Man City again in 2017-18 and Liverpool in 2019-20; each of those teams went on to finish first.

While Arsenal's only loss of the top-flight campaign so far came away to Brighton & Hove Albion, they have won each of their other four road trips without conceding and have also kept four straight clean sheets altogether in the Premier League; not since January 2006 have they registered five straight shut-outs in the division.

Arsenal's four clean sheets in their last four Premier League games is more than Newcastle have managed across all competitions all season, Jaissle's men only keeping the opposition at bay three times and failing to do so at Craven Cottage on November 7.

A Jacob Murphy stunner preceded a slightly fortuitous Rodrigo Muniz equaliser for Fulham, extending Newcastle's winless run to three games in all tournaments and leaving them languishing in the bottom half.

Nevertheless, Jaissle labelled a point in London a "step in the right direction" after his side's harrowing home loss to Everton, as Murphy's fine left-footed strike continued the Magpies' sequence of scoring in every away game in 2026-27.

However, after scoring at least twice in each of their first four matches at St James' Park this season, Newcastle have now failed to net in each of their last two, going down 1-0 to Aston Villa and Everton in successive clashes.

The hosts were also subjected to an agonising one-goal loss in this fixture last term, as Gabriel Magalhaes completed a 2-1 Arsenal comeback win, ending the Gunners' three-match losing run in front of the St James' Park faithful.

Newcastle United Premier League form:.

Newcastle United form (all competitions):.

Arsenal form (all competitions):.

Arsenal players did not drop like flies over the international break, contrary to some previous pauses, but the Gunners are likely to be without Martin Zubimendi after the midfielder appeared to hurt his hamstring in Spain's 3-2 loss to England.

The second-string lynchpin joins Bukayo Saka (quad) and the suspended Max Dowman on the Arsenal sidelines, but Arteta will otherwise have an identical squad to the one that got the better of Hull.

Expect Bruno Guimaraes to appear from the off against his former employers, while Havertz should hold off the threat of Viktor Gyokeres despite the latter extending an all-time Nations League record in November.

On Newcastle's end, Jacob Ramsey returns from a one-match ban after his sending-off against Everton, while Nico Gonzalez and Joe Willock are also expected to be fine despite suffering from illness earlier in the week.

Joelinton's thigh injury will likely keep him out of this one, though, while backup goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen will be out for at least another few weeks with a hamstring problem of his own.

Ex-Arsenal target Matias Fernandez-Pardo has also returned from a troublesome illness of his own, and the 21-year-old may be given a shot over the underwhelming Yoane Wissa here.

Newcastle United possible starting lineup:.

Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall; Steur, Gonzalez; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Osula.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

While the break came at a better time for Newcastle than Arsenal, an increasingly familiar fate is set to befall the Magpies at St James' Park.

The champions' defensive might is showing no sign of wavering, nor is their ability to grind out victories in challenging circumstances, so we anticipate another 1-0 to the Arsenal.

West Ham Stadium Concert Decision Raises Questions Over £15m Forecast

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this week, Newham Council resolved to grant planning permission for changes that will enable the London Stadium to host more major concerts and entertainment events.
  • “The decision by Newham Council represents a significant milestone in the Stadium’s ambition to attract more world-class entertainment and sporting events to East London, delivering increased opportunities for visitors, businesses and the local community.”.
  • The permission will allow London Stadium to increase its annual allocation of concerts and other non-sporting leisure events from 10 to 24, alongside the ability to host up to eight events each year at a maximum capacity of 85,000.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this week, Newham Council resolved to grant planning permission for changes that will enable the London Stadium to host more major concerts and entertainment events.

London Stadium released a statement saying:.

“The decision by Newham Council represents a significant milestone in the Stadium’s ambition to attract more world-class entertainment and sporting events to East London, delivering increased opportunities for visitors, businesses and the local community.”.

The permission will allow London Stadium to increase its annual allocation of concerts and other non-sporting leisure events from 10 to 24, alongside the ability to host up to eight events each year at a maximum capacity of 85,000.

There will be no changes to West Ham United’s fixtures or the club’s current matchday capacity of 62,500. No physical changes to the stadium are required.

The application was supported by an economic impact assessment forecasting the potential to generate an additional £15 million for the Newham economy through up to 800,000 additional visits to the stadium each year.

Newly introduced London Stadium CEO Darren Raczkowski mentioned:.

“This is a hugely positive outcome for London Stadium and for East London. We are delighted that Newham Council has recognised the opportunity these changes present, both for the Stadium and the wider local economy.”.

However, on closer scrutiny, you have to ask what the point of increasing to 24 days is and whether the claimed benefits will ever be realised.

Before planning permission was granted, the London Stadium could host up to 10 days of concerts each year, a limit it has never reached in the ten years since opening.

To date, since 2016, no more than five days (half the previous planning permission allowance for concerts) have been used in any single year, so the change seems a bit of wishful thinking to go over ten and reach the dizzy heights of 24 days.

The cost of hosting concerts outside the summer break, while the seats are moved, is likely to be prohibitive. The cost of moving seats remains in the millions, and laying out protective flooring for one concert in an international break could make the venue commercially unattractive, even if the seats remained in place.

Sources indicate that the concert venue marketplace is competitive, with Wembley, the O2, Spurs Stadium and Emirates. Brentford are also looking to use their Gtech Community Stadium for future concerts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

Recent findings suggest that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson noted, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

In a recent development, any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

Industry observers note that “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

According to recent reports, alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola remarked, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose mentioned. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola remarked: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that highlighted why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

"That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young stated on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

Recent findings suggest that his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has mentioned and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has noted that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

According to recent reports, adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his significant move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Carlo Ancelotti is likely to remain Brazil head coach until at least the 2028 Copa America, regardless of Pep Guardiola's availability, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery.
  • The Italian is under growing pressure after a turbulent November window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 19 Nov 2026 09:18.

Carlo Ancelotti is likely to remain Brazil head coach until at least the 2028 Copa America, regardless of Pep Guardiola's availability, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery.

The Italian is under growing pressure after a turbulent November window. He was sent off during Saturday's 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan, prompting Brazil great Romario to publicly demand his exit, before watching from the stands as his side thrashed Singapore 7-0 on Tuesday.

That followed a hugely disappointing World Cup, in which Brazil were knocked out in the last 16 by Norway, their earliest exit from the tournament since 1990.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery admitted that Ancelotti's reign has fallen well short of expectations, but believes his contract, which runs until 2030, is keeping him in the job.

"If this was a run-of-the-mill Brazil coach, he could well already be receiving his marching orders, because there's no doubt about it: his time with Brazil has proved a massive disappointment so far," Vickery said.

"Through the World Cup it was acceptable and nothing more until, by his own confession, he made a very poor substitution against Norway and lost control of that game.

In a recent development, "Coming off an extremely disappointing World Cup, Brazilians want to win. They're not that patient, and they're not that interested in long-term tests.

"The key problem is one he hasn't solved: how do you reconcile a team with two wingers with the midfield resources Brazil have, and still remain compact and defensively solid?".

Guardiola has been out of work since leaving Manchester City at the end of 2025-26, and he has history with the Selecao. In late 2012, while on sabbatical in New York, he let it be known that coaching Brazil was the one job that could tempt him back, only for the CBF to rush through the appointment of Luiz Felipe Scolari.

Vickery believes Brazil would now be more open to Guardiola, but stressed that no change is imminent, with Ancelotti's next opportunity to impress not coming until the end of March.

Industry observers note that "As a club coach, if things aren't going well, you try something on Wednesday and something else at the weekend. You can't do that as a national team coach," Vickery explained.

"The pressure is on him to come up with a coherent idea of a side, and if that means packing the midfield and giving up one of his wingers, that's the way he's going to have to go.

"The next international window is very important for him to win his credibility back, but I suspect at least until the Copa America of 2028, Carlo Ancelotti will be Brazil coach.".

Guardiola has also been tipped to replace Mauricio Pochettino as USA manager following the latter's move to Manchester United, and Pochettino has publicly talked up the ex-Manchester City boss taking the job.

One Liverpool player has been praised for his ‘brilliant’ performance for his country on Tuesday night.

Hungary’s two UEFA Nations League matches over the past week have been overshadowed by the fallout from Dominik Szoboszlai admitting that he played through the pain barrier for his country, a decision which hasn’t gone down well among some on Merseyside.

His club and international teammate Milos Kerkez was also in action for Marco Rossi’s side at home to Northern Ireland last night, and the 23-year-old’s efforts didn’t go unnoticed among the media.

Hungarian football writer Bence Bocsak took to X shortly after the final whistle in Budapest, where the match finished in a 1-1 draw, to praise the Liverpool left-back’s performance.

He posted: ‘Milos Kerkez was brilliant for Hungary tonight. The Liverpool man created the most chances in the game (4) and won the most tackles (2). Also won 6/7 duels and made 10 passes into the final third – the most on the pitch.’.

(Photo by David Balogh/Getty Images).

While there was frustration for Kerkez and Szoboszlai over the result, which saw the Magyars miss their shot at automatic promotion to League A and instead face a two-legged play-off next March, the Liverpool defender can be especially pleased with his own contribution on Tuesday.

The figures below from Sofascore – some of which were also cited by Bocsak – illustrate the combative and creative attributes that the 23-year-old highlighted for Hungary last night.

Kerkez has started the bulk of our Premier League matches so far this season, even if at times he can still be overly impetuous to the extent that, after an accidental collision with Florian Wirtz against Bournemouth in September, Jamie Carragher described him as ‘a bit mad’.

However, he should take heart from his strong outing for his country, and Liverpool will need him to be even more assured and influential when Manchester United come to Anfield on Sunday.

It’d be the perfect occasion for our number 6 to deliver a statement performance and show that he can mature into being an integral presence in Andoni Iraola’s project on Merseyside.

According to recent reports, in Episode 18 of The Mag Pod, we find Jamie, Simon, and Hutch reflecting back on the time of Covid and a pre-Newcastle United takeover era that featured Steve Bruce, Mike Ashley and Joe Willock. A strange time indeed to be a United fan.

You can play episode 18 on the audio player above or use your favourite podcast platforms including Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, YouTube, and Acast.

Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! Join Jamie, Simon, and Hutch for unfiltered football debate.

Newcastle United’s difficult 2020-21 season under Steve Bruce, Joe Willock’s remarkable loan spell and the build-up to the Saudi-backed takeover are the focus as Jamie Smith, Simon Cahill and David Hutchinson return for the final instalment of their international break specials.

The trio revisit football behind closed doors, compare the pre-takeover squad with today’s Newcastle United and look ahead to the return of Bruno Guimarães with Arsenal.

Industry observers note that the 2020-21 campaign was a strange time to be a Newcastle supporter. With St James’ Park largely empty due to Covid restrictions, Mike Ashley still in charge and Steve Bruce overseeing some desperately uninspiring football, the connection between supporters and their club was arguably at its lowest point.

Simon takes us back through the season, from the arrival of Callum Wilson and Ryan Fraser to the struggles of a side relying heavily on Allan Saint-Maximin for attacking inspiration. Despite spending much of the campaign uncomfortably close to the relegation places, Newcastle eventually finished 12th, thanks in no small part to Joe Willock’s extraordinary impact after joining on loan from Arsenal.

There’s also a moving personal story from Simon about his family’s experiences during lockdown, providing a reminder that football was only one part of an extraordinary period in everyone’s lives.

The discussion then turns to the present.

Has Newcastle’s squad improved as much as it should have since the takeover? Are there players from Bruce’s team who would strengthen today’s starting eleven? And how much patience should supporters have with the club’s latest recruits?

With the international break finally ending, there’s a round up of Newcastle players representing their countries before attention switches to Arsenal’s visit and the potentially awkward reception awaiting former Magpies favourite Bruno Guimarães.

Plenty of nostalgia, disagreement and the usual irreverent humour in another edition of The Mag Pod.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United manager Scott Parker has identified defensive positioning, transitions and set pieces as areas he intends to improve following the international break.
  • West Ham are the Championship’s highest scorers, but their defensive record has repeatedly undermined their attacking performances.
  • Personally, I’ve always thought there were some relatively easy wins for Parker in terms of fixing West Ham’s defensive problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has identified defensive positioning, transitions and set pieces as areas he intends to improve following the international break. Speaking to talkSPORT this morning, the Hammers boss explained why his team must become more disciplined without sacrificing their attacking ambition.

West Ham are the Championship’s highest scorers, but their defensive record has repeatedly undermined their attacking performances. Parker acknowledged that committing players forward can leave his side exposed, particularly when possession changes hands, and stressed the importance of what his players do behind the ball.

Personally, I’ve always thought there were some relatively easy wins for Parker in terms of fixing West Ham’s defensive problems. We’re scoring plenty of goals; we just need to sort the defence out. And if there’s one thing Parker has demonstrated during his managerial career, it’s that he knows how to organise a team defensively.

During his time at Burnley, Parker oversaw one of the most remarkable defensive campaigns in English football history.

His side conceded just 16 goals across 46 Championship matches during the 2024/25 season, setting a newly introduced record and keeping 30 clean sheets on their way to promotion.

Speaking in his talkSPORT interview, Parker discussed the importance of positioning when West Ham commit players forward, explaining that transitions and set pieces are particularly dangerous in the Championship.

And it’s interesting to hear him targeting transitions because that was exactly how West Ham conceded the opening goal against Blackburn Rovers in our last game.

Parker has informed West Ham players that they are now Championship players whether they like it or not.

But perhaps the most interesting part of Parker’s interview was his frank assessment of the mentality required from players who have dropped out of the Premier League.

He pointed out that the demands of the Championship are completely different, with players needing to accept the physical and psychological challenges of the division.

Parker then delivered a particularly pointed observation.

“If there’s a player here at this present moment in time playing in this division, it’s because that’s where he is.”.

It was a way of saying that irrespective of where you come from, it’s where you are that counts.

And no doubt there are players in the West Ham squad who consider themselves to be Premier League, European or international quality.

However, as of right now, they are Championship players, and Parker is quite right to point that out.

The upcoming gaffer has been promoted from this division three times, so I suspect he knows rather more about what is required than some of the players who have spent most of their careers in the Premier League.

Of course, the international break has given Parker a welcome opportunity to work with his players, although it’s crucial to remember that ten were away representing their countries.

Nevertheless, he will have learned considerably more about those who remained at Rush Green.

In particular, players such as full-backs Ezra Mayers and Joël Veltman have had the opportunity to work with the upcoming manager, while a good number of West Ham’s midfielders have also remained at the club.

That should have allowed Parker to concentrate on some of the defensive positioning and tactical habits he discussed during the interview.

And let’s not forget that he’ll also have Thursday and Friday’s training sessions to work with his returning internationals ahead of Preston.

That is considerably more preparation time than he enjoyed before his opening two matches against Cardiff and Blackburn.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sunderland boss Regis le Bris has revealed that at least five Sunderland players could miss the derby match against Newcastle United at St James’ Park.

That game is in 17 days time on Sunday 6 December with a 2pm kick-off.

Regis le Bris announcing on Thursday that all five of these Sunderland players will miss the Premier League away game at Villa Park on Saturday.

The quintet that definitely miss the weekend’s Aston Villa away game are Brian Brobbey, Dan Ballard, Granit Xhaka, Romaine Mundle and Habib Diarra.

Two of these five Sunderland players will for sure miss the Newcastle United game, Regis le Bris saying today: “Daniel Ballard and Romaine Mundle will be back training in mid-December.”.

The way the Sunderland manager was speaking, it appears very unlikely that Brian Brobbey or Granit Xhaka will be available for the derby.

On Brian Brobbey, Regis le Bris saying today: “It is a substantial injury for Brian, which we will have to assess weekly. It is a fresh injury for us but it is too early to know the timeline. He is sad and disappointed because he has worked so hard. He was a monster against Chelsea, so I think it is important for us and him to reset. I hope that he will use this period to get better.”.

As for Granit Xhaka, Regis le Bris stating he won’t be back until after Brian Brobbey: “For Granit it is a bit longer, it is a calf injury.”.

The only one of the five Sunderland players who appears to have any kind of realistic chance of featuring in the Newcastle United match is Habib Diarra.

With Regis le Bris explaining: “For Habib Diarra it is going well and we will see in the next two weeks or so.”.

West Ham United’s Championship promotion hopes may have received an unexpected boost following confirmation that Swansea City manager Vítor Matos has left the Welsh club to take charge of French side Strasbourg.

Recent findings suggest that the Portuguese coach had established Swansea as genuine promotion contenders, with the Swans sitting sixth in the Championship. His departure comes at an awkward time for a club attempting to maintain its challenge near the top of the table.

Recent findings suggest that strasbourg officially appointed Matos on Wednesday evening, replacing Hugo Oliveira. And whilst there’s no guarantee Swansea will suffer without him, I certainly regard this as good news for West Ham.

Matos was an extremely capable manager who had Swansea punching well above their weight.

Industry observers note that when he arrived in November 2025, Swansea were languishing in 20th position. He eventually guided them to an 11th-place finish before establishing them amongst the promotion contenders this season.

The destination has turned out to be Strasbourg rather than Selhurst Park, but the potential consequences for Swansea remain much the same.

From a West Ham perspective, I’ll certainly take it.

Liverpool have been handed a significant double injury boost in the days leading up to their Premier League clash against Manchester United.

Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.

The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.

As reported by Paul Joyce for The Times, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to Liverpool first-team training, with both defenders having been sidelined for a number of months with serious knee injuries.

The Northern Ireland right-back has been out of action since January after he was struck down towards the end of the 0-0 draw at Arsenal; while the Italian teenager has been absent for even longer, not playing since rupturing his ACL on his Reds debut in September 2025.

The latter had been due to resume full training in early October before that staging post was delayed as medical staff took a cautious approach, but he’s now in the final stages of his recovery to full fitness and could resume playing in the coming weeks.

While we wouldn’t bank on either of the Liverpool duo returning to matchday action in the concluding weeks of 2026, their resumption of first-team training comes as a huge step towards their long-awaited comebacks.

Bradley would very likely have made the right-back position his own this season had he not been sidelined, but thankfully Ronald Araujo has excelled in that role since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

As for Leoni, it was beyond cruel that he tore his ACL towards the end of what had been a terrific Reds debut against Southampton 14 months ago, but he’s still only 19 and should hopefully have a hugely successful career still ahead of him.

Even when both players are cleared for a return to action, it’ll take time for them to properly get back into a matchday rhythm, and Iraola will surely bed them in gently after missing so much football over the past few months.

However, having them back in a full training feels like a significant step forward, and when the time comes for them to resume playing, it’ll be a wonderful sight for everyone associated with Liverpool.

West Ham Could Save Themselves A Transfer Fee

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that recent reports linking West Ham with Bristol City goalkeeper Joe Duncan are understandable.
  • But while Duncan is undoubtedly a talented young goalkeeper, West Ham must ask a simple question: why spend time, money and resources pursuing another developing keeper when they already have one of the country’s most highly-rated young goalkeepers sitting in their own academy?
  • Recent findings suggest that finlay Herrick joined the club at the age of six and has progressed through every level of the academy system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that recent reports linking West Ham with Bristol City goalkeeper Joe Duncan are understandable. The 20-year-old has enjoyed an impressive loan spell at Southend United, earned a surprise senior Wales call-up and is attracting attention from a number of clubs.

But while Duncan is undoubtedly a talented young goalkeeper, West Ham must ask a simple question: why spend time, money and resources pursuing another developing keeper when they already have one of the country’s most highly-rated young goalkeepers sitting in their own academy?

Recent findings suggest that finlay Herrick joined the club at the age of six and has progressed through every level of the academy system. He was part of the famous side that won the FA Youth Cup and U18 Premier League South double in 2022/23, signed a long-term contract in 2024 and has represented England from U16 through to U20 level. Herrick, now aged 20, has already made three senior appearances for West Ham.

The standout moment came in the FA Cup quarter-final against Leeds United when he replaced Alphonse Areola in the 120th minute and immediately saved a penalty in the shootout. Although the Hammers ultimately lost, Herrick demonstrated the composure and personality required to perform under intense pressure.

He also acquitted himself well in the EFL second-round 4-1 win at Southampton back in August.

According to recent reports, in his last game, three saves, including a vital one-on-one against Fulham, were not enough as we were edged out of the EFL Cup 3-2 by our London rivals. However, our young custodian blamed himself for the third goal, saying he needed to be harsh on himself and should have done better to prevent it.

Regarding Duncan, he has come through Bristol City’s academy and gained valuable experience on loan at Tiverton Town and Farnborough before stepping up to National League football with Southend United. His performances have been good enough to earn a Wales senior squad call-up from Craig Bellamy despite never making a first-team appearance for Bristol City.

Southend manager Kieron Dyer and Bellamy have both spoken positively about his development, while West Ham are reportedly among several clubs monitoring his situation.

One of the biggest criticisms supporters have of modern football is that clubs often look elsewhere rather than trusting their own youth products. You only have to look at former academy prospect Nathan Trott, who was regularly loaned out to other clubs and has now quickly established himself as the main keeper for Cardiff City.

According to recent reports, behind Herrick are a number of other keepers coming through the ranks, with high expectations of Lanre Awesu, who at just 18 years old has featured for the U21 side on a number of occasions. Standing at 6ft 5in, he has been highly praised by David Martin, along with fellow keeper Finley Hooper.

Herrick has already spent 14 years at the club. He has excelled at youth level, earned England recognition, performed well on loan and shown promise when given an opportunity with the senior side.

At some point, development becomes about opportunity.

If a goalkeeper with Herrick’s pedigree cannot move up the pecking order, then what is the purpose of the academy pathway? What message does that give to Herrick, Awesu and Hooper?

With Hermansen failing to convince and Areola proving increasingly unreliable due to injuries, the moment for Herrick could arrive far quicker than anyone anticipated.

In my opinion, the Hammers should show faith in their own. The smartest signing West Ham can make may already be wearing number 49 at Rush Green!

Latest Update: I think this is the best Newcastle United team that is available now

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has not been an enjoyable season watching the Newcastle United team so far and that’s being nice about, it may be hyperbolic to say we’ve been as bad as some of what we saw under the dark days of Mike Ashley, but the cluelessness of our play at times this year has definitely brought up memories of John Carver and Steve Bruce for me.
  • For the record, I think persisting with a manager who is making Ruben Amorim seem flexible isn’t a great idea, but trying to think of how with the current squad we might be able to make the best of the situation.
  • Industry observers note that let us start with the issues for Matthias Jaissle’ s preferred system, firstly at the back where being honest I think our back five who started against Fulham are ok together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has not been an enjoyable season watching the Newcastle United team so far and that’s being nice about, it may be hyperbolic to say we’ve been as bad as some of what we saw under the dark days of Mike Ashley, but the cluelessness of our play at times this year has definitely brought up memories of John Carver and Steve Bruce for me.

For the record, I think persisting with a manager who is making Ruben Amorim seem flexible isn’t a great idea, but trying to think of how with the current squad we might be able to make the best of the situation.

Industry observers note that let us start with the issues for Matthias Jaissle’ s preferred system, firstly at the back where being honest I think our back five who started against Fulham are ok together. Hornicek has made a few mistakes but overall, he’s made some good saves, and his ball playing is a significant help.

At LB Lewis Hall is an absolute Unicorn and could play in any system, at RB Dedic is a bit defensively suspect but has a lot of energy and gets up and down the line. CB is where the theoretical problem is, Jaissles system requires pacy ball playing CBs, who are good when left 1v1 and the only one of ours who fits that bill in some way is Thiaw, who is generally great but has the odd Titus moment.

Our other CBs just aren’t fits in this system, none have the pace, Schar is fading a bit even on the ball and Botman has never been the same since our medical staff got their hands on him. I’m not that worried about this area of the pitch too much though as despite Dan Burn being slow and not the greatest on the ball he won’t overplay, and he will put his body on the line and win as much as he can. I think there is always a place for an old school CB. So, keep that back five from the Fulham game together and we should be ok there.

Now moving into midfield and we need two for the double pivot, Joelinton gives you physically but he doesn’t have the guile or composure required to play there week in and week out (though what I’d give to have him vs Arsenal on Saturday). Ramsey is pretty anonymous there, Willock despite once every few years looking like he could be a great destroyer (Hull this season and the first half vs Forest (4-3) a couple of years ago) is way too inconsistent and finally Bamba who looks lost in his limited minutes and has hardly had a look in.

Industry observers note that as such, it comes down for me to two of three, we have Nico who’s shown his quality in a couple of games (Palace/Spurs) but has ran around and fouled a lot in others, Miley who can look like a world beater but then also get overran and finally Steur who’s great on the ball but has defensive limitations at this point in his development. All three lack legs but from what we have they are definitely our best options.

According to recent reports, I think when thinking of who is best in the double pivot we need to think of who is going to be in the 10 with them. So far this year it has been Wissa and Willock there the most with the odd moment of Ramsey.

In a recent development, wissa after one good game against Liverpool looks like he’s put his jeans back on and just isn’t suitable, Willock has his moments but like in the pivot he’s incredibly inconsistent and can coast for larger parts of the game and finally Ramsey while not seeming like an awful player has so little impact. I think going for him rather than El Khannouss will be one that bites us far years.

Sources indicate that so, not an inspiring group of options in that 10 role which is key to this system working, we need someone dropping between the lines, who can then turn and make quick accurate passes to our front line. None of the three mentioned can do that at any sort of decent level and it kills our attacking play. I do think we have one player who could thrive here.

According to recent reports, that player is Sean Steur whose passing range is probably the best we have and his footballing brain belies his years. You may think it’s not his position. he plays deeper and he’s very good there, and to that I say we need to look to the south coast and to Brighton and one of this season’s best players in Pascal Gross.

According to recent reports, you see Gross often lines up as the 10 for Brighton and his passing ability and nous causes chaos but he doesn’t just stay at the top end of the field, he has freedom to wander and drop deep and start attacks. I can see Steur not only being able to do this but be able to thrive in this role. The added bonus is as we have two other midfielders behind him his defensive limitations are covered.

Because of this, in the middle of the pitch I’d want to see Steur in the 10 and Miley and Nico in the double pivot, there is a risk of not having a runner in there but you’d hope with the technical ability of those three we can exert a degree of control on games and set a firmer base in front of the defence.

We then move to the wingers, where in Jaissle’s systems the wingers need to be comfortable coming inside and creating space for the full-backs to overlap leading to overloads of the opposition defence. One of our massive problems is on the right-hand side we have two wingers who being polite are touchline wingers and being more blunt, Jacob Murphy puts in the occasional good ball but his all-round game is chronic and Elanga reminds me of Obertan and not because of the pace (I’m waiting for him to forget to take the ball with him when he’s running through at some point).

On the left Barnes always puts up a good stat line but his unwillingness to have a go at full-backs combined with his low success rate of beating his man puts us on the back foot a lot. The one thing Barnes does well is he makes a lot of runs, maybe with someone in that ten who can find him he would offer more.

Toure is so raw if he were a steak a Frenchman would send him back to cook some more, he has moments, but you just don’t know what you would get with him. I’d be tempted to play him more purely because he is one of our only options who will get at his full-back and I think he may actually be better playing on the right in the long run.

Recent findings suggest that the last player to throw into the mix is Pardo, the lad wants to be a striker but that is very optimistic, and I think it’s clear he’s a winger and that’s where he needs to play most likely on the left. So again, on the wings not an inspiring bunch, I’d like to see Pardo getting game time on the left and it’s between Toure or Barnes for the right (Murphy and Elanga only look good when the other is playing). I think it would have to be Toure as we need to see what he can do, he’s a left footer so would cut inside more naturally, and he can make something happen.

According to recent reports, the last position is probably the most worrying because at previous clubs Matthias Jaissle has used strikers like Toney and Sesko as his focal points, physical centre forwards who can put pressure on the opposition centre backs and hold the ball up. As mentioned before, Wissa often looks like he is playing in Jeans and even when he gets on the ball, he has been less than inspiring and doesn’t have the physicality to hold the ball up or the quality to link the play up. Our other option is Osula who can be chaotic and has moments where you think there might be a player there but then he does things like not run in a straight line when chasing a pass or get shrugged off the ball despite his physical gifts. There’s something there but he has a very headless vibe. At this point he’s clearly the better option but if Wilson gets his act together and does something in January a CF is a must.

So, for now a 4-2-3-1 Newcastle United team of:.

Hornicek, Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall, Nico, Miley, Toure, Steur, Pardo, Osula.

This is what I think is the best we’ve got and I’d like to see this line up at some point soon, but I think the key thing we need to try is moving Steur into the free/10 role, to let him try and solve our creativity concerns.

It has been revealed that anyway, back to reality and Saturday coming, fingers crossed for the oncoming onslaught of the Opulent Stoke. Fingers crossed and Howay the Mags.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:15.

Aiming to further strengthen their survival bid, Notts County welcome playoff-chasing Stevenage to Meadow Lane for an all-crucial League One clash on Saturday afternoon.

The Magpies enjoyed a promising unbeaten run prior to the November international break, whilst the Boro also experienced success in both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy.

For the first time since the 2014-15 campaign, Notts County are back in the third tier of English football, with the East Midlanders aiming to avoid a season of bottom-four struggle in League One.

Since a 2-0 defeat by Wycombe Wanderers on October 17, the Magpies have strung together a five-game unbeaten run (W4 D1) across third tier, FA Cup and EFL Trophy action, including a 3-0 away success at Burton Albion in the latter competition on November 10.

After collecting a commendable tally of seven points from their past three third-tier contests, Notts County have moved up to 18th position in the League One standings, two points above the relegation spaces.

A worrying statistic ahead of Saturday afternoon, only Peterborough United (5), Barnsley (5) and whipping boys Bromley (5) have earned fewer than the Magpies' eight home points in the division so far.

Head coach Martin Paterson was heralded as a hero after guiding Notts County to League Two playoff victory during this first campaign in charge, however, the former Tampa Bay Rowdies assistant now faces a different type of task at a higher level of the English pyramid.

Just days before the announcement of his contract extension, Stevenage captain Carl Piergianni netted the only goal of the Kassam Stadium contest to knock Oxford United out of the FA Cup at the first-round stage.

At the beginning of the following week, the Boro enjoyed an EFL Trophy win over Fulham Under-21s, meaning that Alex Revell's troops were three games unbeaten (W2 D1) across all competitions heading into the November pause.

Stevenage were losing semi-finalists to Stockport County in last season's playoffs, and the Hertfordshire outfit are currently way off the top-six pace, sitting seven points behind sixth-placed Plymouth Argyle.

Following Jamie Reid's summer switch to divisional rivals Reading, the Boro have shared the goalscoring responsibilities amongst their ranks, with Dan Kemp, Josh Magennis and Oliver Sanderson all netting on three occasions in League One so far.

Due to Notts County's recent plights in non-league and League Two, Saturday's meeting at Meadow Lane will be the first between the two sides since March 2019, with the Magpies unbeaten in their past four battles (W2 D2) against Stevenage dating back to November 2017.

Both returning from international duty with Republic of Ireland Under-21s, Darius Lipsiuc and Rory Finneran could feature this weekend for Notts County.

Back from two substitute appearances for Sierra Leone in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying, Charlton Athletic loanee Daniel Kanu is looking for his seventh League One start of the term.

Nicholas Tsaroulla has spent time away on Nations League duty for Cyprus and could be an option in the middle of the park or at wing-back for the Magpies at Meadow Lane.

Scoring for Stevenage in the most recent league match at Leicester City on October 31, Ben Broggio and Tugra Turhan are pushing for starts.

There is still plenty of experience within the Boro ranks, though, with Northern Irishman Magennis and midfielder Louis Thompson expected to make the XI.

Belshaw; Ness, McDonald, Bedeau; Tsaroulla, Finneran, Robertson, Samuels-Smith; Roberts; Kanu, Smyth.

Unbeaten against Stevenage since March 2017, Notts County should be confident of extending their positive run at Meadow Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Boro have won just one of their opening six away league trips this term and are likely to struggle in the East Midlands.

Preston manager Graham Alexander confirmed the extent of the injury in an interview with the Lancashire Evening Post, having lost Kenny during the defeat to Sheffield United earlier this month. The striker’s absence adds to Preston’s injury problems ahead of their visit to the London Stadium.

However, Preston have already demonstrated they can win without Kenny, having beaten Southampton in their previous fixture. Midfielder Léo Leroy is also available again after suspension, although captain Ali McCann remains sidelined.

Parker has already shown that he’s prepared to use Magassa, having recalled him for the Cardiff City match.

It’s a possibility we’ve previously discussed when examining Parker’s looks for the international break, and the manager has now had considerably more time to work on his tactical approach.

Kenny’s absence is undoubtedly welcome news for West Ham, but it won’t dictate Parker’s team selection.

Whether that results in a starting place against Preston remains to be seen.

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

In a recent development, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville notes Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

Industry observers note that it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

It has been revealed that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

According to recent reports, that 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

Industry observers note that it was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so notable for us.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

Sources indicate that the script pretty much writes itself these days. Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager noted.

Industry observers note that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty substantial one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty significant one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and upcoming head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Industry observers note that fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

Premier League KMI Panel unanimously admits to another refereeing error which wronged Liverpool

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (535 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.
  • The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.
  • The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (476 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

West Ham United v Preston North End EFL Championship London Stadium Saturday 21 November 2026, 3pm GMT.

Sources indicate that scott Parker’s first home match as West Ham United head coach is massively notable. Preston North End are bottom of the Championship and, while Saturday’s fixture is not mathematically must-win, realistically it feels very close to it.

West Ham have collected one point from Parker’s opening two games and must start closing the gap to the automatic-promotion places. After two uninterrupted weeks with much of his squad, this is the first proper opportunity to judge whether the newly introduced head coach has begun improving the organisation and intensity of the team.

Recent findings suggest that there is also the troubling matter of West Ham’s home form. I worried before relegation that the vast gaps between the London Stadium crowd and the pitch might turn it into a disadvantage rather than an advantage, and we now desperately need to begin winning there consistently.

The London Stadium has not remotely resembled a fortress this season. Opponents have arrived believing they can frustrate West Ham, exploit the anxiety around the ground and capitalise when the players become nervous.

As one former Championship striker recently observed, visiting teams have been enjoying the London Stadium experience. That situation has to change if West Ham are serious about challenging for automatic promotion.

Parker needs his players to begin rapidly and give the crowd something to respond to. The longer this remains goalless, the more Preston will believe their long-ball approach and deep defensive shape can earn them something.

Scott Parker will need to make the London Stadium feel like home.

According to recent reports, west Ham will dominate possession, so the challenge will be using it properly. Passing sideways in front of an organised defence will achieve very little; we need quicker movement, runners beyond the striker and enough tempo to pull Preston out of position.

Industry observers note that I expect West Ham to be considerably tighter defensively following Parker’s first extended spell on the training pitch. However, the international break has not been quite as useful as it initially appeared because several important players were away representing their countries.

Industry observers note that konstantinos Mavropanos was among those absent, while Max Kilman is suspended after reaching the disciplinary threshold at Blackburn. Parker has therefore been unable to work throughout the fortnight with the central-defensive partnership he will need on Saturday.

I suspect Morato will move into his natural centre-back position alongside Mavropanos. That is probably the safe and predictable selection, although I would prefer to see Airidas Golambeckis given the opportunity.

The teenager has generally impressed when called upon and deserves serious consideration. As our examination of Parker’s defensive conundrum against Preston highlighted, the decision appears to be between Morato’s experience and Golambeckis’ encouraging performances.

Joël Veltman should start at right-back, while Ezra Mayers deserves to retain his place on the left. Kyle Walker-Peters continues to be assessed, but Parker has two natural and capable full-back options without needing to rush him back.

According to recent reports, the biggest selection question surrounds the goalkeeper. I am finding Parker’s team difficult to predict primarily because I do not know whether he will retain Mads Hermansen or turn to Alphonse Areola.

According to recent reports, hermansen has produced an inconsistent sequence of performances. He excelled for Denmark against Portugal before making another clanger during the defeat by Norway, which will not have made Parker’s decision any easier.

According to recent reports, there has been considerable pressure for West Ham to make a change in goal, but Areola’s own fitness has reportedly been an problem. Until Parker confirms otherwise, my best guess is that Hermansen will retain his place.

I suspect Parker will stick with Hermansen.

In a recent development, this is an ideal fixture in which to rebuild the goalkeeper’s confidence, but Preston’s likely use of long balls and set pieces means he must command his penalty area properly. Another nervous display would only intensify the debate but my own choice would be to select Finn Herrick.

I expect Parker to continue with the 4-2-3-1 formation. Arne Engels and Soungoutou Magassa should form the central-midfield partnership, with Divine Mukasa operating further forward.

Magassa gives West Ham a recognised holding midfielder and should help protect a changed defence. That will allow Engels to move the ball forward and support Mukasa rather than both central midfielders occupying similar positions.

In a recent development, preston’s victory over Southampton was built around an aggressive pressing approach, something Parker will have worked on during the break. I previously argued that West Ham must learn to play through Preston’s press, and this midfield should contain enough composure and energy to do it.

Jarrod Bowen will naturally start on the right, with Edvin Austbø on the left. In my opinion, Austbø has moved ahead of Manor Solomon in the pecking order and deserves a proper run in the team.

According to recent reports, joël Piroe should lead the attack. Parker needs to give West Ham’s most proven Championship goalscorer an extended opportunity rather than continually rotating strikers who have struggled to find any rhythm.

Sources indicate that I expect five players who were away on international duty—Hermansen, Mavropanos, Mukasa, Austbø and Piroe—to start. The key defensive change should see Morato move inside to replace the suspended Kilman.

According to recent reports, preston earned their first victory under Graham Alexander by beating Southampton before the international break, so they should arrive with renewed confidence. However, both of their Championship wins this season have come at home.

According to recent reports, their away record is dreadful. Preston are winless on the road, having drawn once and lost six of their seven away league matches, including some heavy defeats.

It has been revealed that I expect them to use plenty of long balls, remain compact and try to frustrate West Ham. Even so, the Hammers have far better players and will enjoy the lion’s share of possession.

It has been revealed that quite frankly, it is time they highlighted the difference in quality. If West Ham cannot beat the Championship’s bottom club at home after Parker has been given two weeks to prepare, serious questions will remain about our promotion credentials.

According to recent reports, preston may make the opening stages awkward, but West Ham should eventually have far too much attacking quality. Parker’s team need to play with intensity, move the ball promptly and turn possession into genuine chances rather than merely dominating the statistics.

It has been revealed that I expect a much more organised performance following the international break. Preston’s direct approach may still produce a goal, particularly with West Ham fielding a changed central defence, but this should be the afternoon Parker claims his first victory.

Prediction: West Ham United 4-1 Preston North End.
