💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.
  • The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026.

Hamilton Academical 1 Ross County 2.

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.

The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

It has been revealed that county, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

It has been revealed that scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so Fresh Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County.

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

According to recent reports, ‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he remarked. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’.

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

It has been revealed that ‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he stated. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’.

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he remarked: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’.

Recent findings suggest that edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

In a recent development, ‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he noted.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek.

Industry observers note that with 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ said Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

Industry observers note that ‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’.

Industry observers note that the Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ said McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

In a recent development, ‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ said McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’.

There was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ remarked Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’.

He added: ‘The newly introduced guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’.

There were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s about loyalty,’ he noted. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’.

A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he noted. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’.

According to recent reports, A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he said. ‘This season we are going up.’.

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game.

Brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

He was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he mentioned. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’.

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he said.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County.

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he said. ‘We are scoring team goals.’.

Has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he said. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’.

Recent findings suggest that it was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he mentioned.

He added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’.

Asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he remarked: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’.

There is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

Borussia Monchengladbach vs Borussia Dortmund - prediction, team news, lineups

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 13:23.

The next instalment of the Borussen derby takes place at Borussia Park when Borussia Dortmund travel to face Borussia Monchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Dortmund come into the clash in second place with 21 points, trailing league-leaders Bayern Munich due to goal difference, whereas the hosts are last in 18th place with just four points.

Gladbach's situation is precarious but not irrecoverable, with the club's tally of four points five fewer than 15th-placed FC Koln, who are the first team outside of the relegation zone.

Head coach Alexander Blessin has only overseen six games as boss, winning twice and losing on three occasions, but his team have taken four points from the last nine on offer in the Bundesliga.

Their latest result was a 3-1 loss against Hamburger SV on November 6, though they did win two and drawn one of their prior three fixtures.

Die Fohlen may ranks as the division's worst defensive team having conceded 25 goals in nine games, but their return of 12 goals in the final third is the second best total in the bottom six.

While Gladbach were defeated in their first three home matches of 2026-27, they have since won once and settled for a stalemate once at Borussia Park, though they are still winless at the ground in the league this season (W0, D1, L3).

Dortmund could find themselves trailing Bayern by three points by the time they face Gladbach due to the fact the Bavarians play against FC Koln on Friday.

Niko Kovac will be delighted by his side's start to the campaign considering 21 points is their joint best tally after nine matchweeks in 13 seasons.

BVB's most recent result was a 2-1 success against Elversberg on November 7, and that was their fifth triumph in six contests.

The club scored at least two goals in five of those fixtures, and though they only managed to keep one clean sheet in that time, no club has conceded fewer goals in the Bundesliga (seven).

Black and Yellow were beaten 1-0 in the corresponding meeting in 2025-26, losing 1-0 at Borussia Park in May, but they emerged victorious in five of their previous six encounters with Gladbach.

Dortmund have taken eight points from a possible 12 on the road in the Bundesliga this term, while they have lost one, drawn two and won just one of their last four outings away from home in all competitions.

Borussia Monchengladbach Bundesliga form:.

Borussia Monchengladbach form (all competitions):.

Borussia Dortmund Bundesliga form:.

Borussia Dortmund form (all competitions):.

Gladbach will have to contend with numerous absences, including suspended centre-back Ko Itakura and injured striker Tim Kleindienst.

Expect to see Kevin Diks, Philipp Sander and Fabio Chiarodia in the backline, while Isac Lidberg may be trusted to lead the line up front.

As for Dortmund, there are still doubts about the availability of centre-forward Serhou Guirassy, who could have to settle for a place on the bench in favour of Fabio Silva.

Jobe Bellingham and Felix Nmecha have often featured together, and they are the most likely duo to start together in a double pivot.

Emre Can is closing in on a return from a cruciate ligament injury, but he is not ready to play on Saturday, so perhaps fans will see a three-man defence consisting of Joane Gadou, Waldemar Anton and Nico Schlotterbeck.

Borussia Monchengladbach possible starting lineup:.

Nicolas; Diks, Sander, Chiarodia; Scally, Uno, Neuhaus, Castrop; Bolin, Lidberg, Mohya.

Borussia Dortmund possible starting lineup:.

Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck; Beier, Bellingham, Nmecha, Svensson; Karetsas, Sabitzer; Silva.

It is difficult to look past Gladbach's poor defensive record given they are the most porous team in the division.

Even if Dortmund fail to keep a clean sheet, there is little evidence to suggest they will suffer a collapse at the back and drop points at Borussia Park.

#2320. Latest Update: The world’s most precious brain samples — and what they teach us about being human

Latest Update: The world’s most precious brain samples — and what they teach us about being human

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2241 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A neuron from the human hippocampus.
  • Neuroscientist Lucy Palmer and her team have been waiting days for this moment.
  • Landmark map of human brain’s gene activity holds clues to Alzheimer’s disease and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A neuron from the human hippocampus. The bushy branches receive signals from other neurons. Credit: Jake Watson and Rebecca Morse-Mora, Jonas group, ISTA.

Neuroscientist Lucy Palmer and her team have been waiting days for this moment.

Landmark map of human brain’s gene activity holds clues to Alzheimer’s disease and more.

Landmark map of human brain’s gene activity holds clues to Alzheimer’s disease and more.

Industry observers note that across the road from her laboratory, at the Royal Melbourne Hospital in Australia, surgeons are removing brain tissue from a person with brain cancer. They set some aside for Palmer to collect and study. It is about the size of a shelled peanut.

A colleague of hers takes the sample, places it in a tub of artificial cerebrospinal fluid and rushes it back to the lab, securing it in a chamber filled with bubbling carbon dioxide and oxygen to keep it alive.

Recent findings suggest that these precious samples can survive for only a day or so before they start to deteriorate, so Palmer’s team wastes no time. Within half an hour of receiving the tissue, they are recording the electrical current passing between neurons as they fire.

Palmer’s group at the Florey Institute in Melbourne is using live brain tissue to understand more about brain cancers and how the activity of neurons influences tumour growth. Her lab, and others using such samples, are doing something rare — measuring how live, working human neurons behave.

Most studies of brain-cell function rely on tissue taken from people who have died or from living animals. Post-mortem human brains, however, preserve only the structure and not the activity of cells, and the brains of other animals might function differently. “As much as we like mice, I don’t want to understand the mouse brain. I want to understand the human brain,” Palmer says.

Sources indicate that slices from a sample of living human brain ready for study.Credit: Emmalyn P. Leonard.

Industry observers note that working with living brain tissue from another person is both humbling and a great privilege, she claims. “Every sample is precious.” It’s also an artisanal skill: attaching recording equipment to individual neurons requires the neuroscientific equivalent of a gardener’s green fingers. It relies on mastery of a decades-old technique called patch-clamping, which has fallen out of fashion as flashier recording methods have become available.

Despite the barriers, there is increasing interest in this rare resource. The number of studies published about this tissue has increased from just a handful two decades ago to upwards of 40 a year, according to data from Scopus, with the bulk attributed to about ten research teams. Neuroscientists around the world are working with surgeons to access the tissue and keep it alive in their labs for periods of time ranging from 24 hours to a few weeks, investigating the intrinsic electrical properties of cells and how they communicate with each other during both health and disease.

“When looking into a disease, being able to look directly at the human tissue is absolutely vital,” says Palmer.

Sources indicate that neuroscientists have many ways to study the human brain: non-invasive scanning, indirect measures such as blood samples and, after death, in slices under the microscope. They can also study brain function directly in animal models and, very rarely, in people who have electrodes implanted while they are undergoing surgery. But none of those approaches allows scientists to measure and manipulate the activity of individual human brain cells in their natural environment.

How to make a brain: upcoming experiments challenge existing picture.

How to make a brain: upcoming experiments challenge existing picture.

According to recent reports, that has changed in the past ten years, states Scott Owen, a neuroscientist at Stanford University in California. Although people have been studying live human tissue since the 1970s, he says, the field has finally reached a point at which enough is known about the mammalian brain to understand how human brains differ from those of other animals.

It has been revealed that his team works with paediatric neurosurgeons to acquire tissue taken from children with epilepsy, cancer or abnormal tangles of blood vessels in their brains. By comparing samples from people with different diseases, the researchers can look for features common to all donors and deduce which are conserved properties of the human brain, rather than artefacts of any one condition.

It has been revealed that in a preprint published in September, for instance, Owen and his colleagues found distinct differences in how human pyramidal neurons — massive, bushy brain cells that live in the cortex — mature compared with those of mice1. The team analysed neocortex samples from 24 children and teenagers, ranging in age from 9 months to 18 years, and mouse samples from equivalent developmental stages. The study, which is yet to be peer reviewed, looked at patterns in how neurons fire, or spike. It’s known that human neurons are quicker to spike after a stimulus than are rodent neurons and that this might correlate with intelligence. Owen and his colleagues found that human neurons got faster at responding over the course of development, with neurons from teens spiking more quickly than those from children; the opposite happened in mice.

Slices from a sample of living human brain, ready for study.Credit: Rennie Kendrick.

When the researchers looked at the genes that might explain how this happens, they found two that increased in expression over time in people, but not in mice. These genes help to create ion channels in cell membranes, which allows signals to travel between neurons. Faults in these genes have been linked to several neurodevelopmental conditions2.

According to recent reports, karri Lämsä, a biophysicist at the Hungarian Centre of Excellence for Molecular Medicine in Szeged, is also interested in how human neurons fire and how these patterns might change with time and newly introduced experiences. His team studies centimetre-wide cubes of the cortex that are discarded during surgeries to enable access to deeper parts of the brain. In a study published last year, they looked at a type of neuron that inhibits others. In these cells, the axon — the main trunk — transmits signals faster and spikes at lower thresholds than in the same cells in mice3. Fast-acting neurons of this type are thought to have a crucial role in complex brain functions.

Sources indicate that lämsä’s team has also been studying how networks of these fast-spiking neurons might change with age. In samples taken from 106 people ranging in age from 11 to 84 years, the researchers found that these circuits become weaker over time and the spikes in electricity travelling across the cell membrane become smaller and slower4. These changes could explain why the human brain becomes less capable of learning and processing information as people age.

It has been revealed that other work using live human tissue has challenged a key assumption about the human brain: that it is a scaled-up version of the mouse brain. Peter Jonas, a neuroscientist at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria in Klosterneuburg, is using live human tissue to understand how brain cells function alone and in networks. Jonas had worked with animal models for more than 30 years when, in 2022, he began collaborating with a neurosurgeon at the Medical University of Vienna. He would receive tiny samples of human brain tissue — mainly from the hippocampus — measuring about one-fifth of a teaspoon.

Industry observers note that can your brain grow upcoming neurons? How researchers are solving a century-old puzzle.

Can your brain grow new neurons? How researchers are solving a century-old puzzle.

His lab’s work suggests that some properties of the human brain, such as the number of dendritic spines (tiny outgrowths at the end of synapses that connect neurons), follow different scaling rules from those of the mouse. Neurons are also more densely connected in the human neocortex — the area of the brain thought to control higher functions such as decision-making and planning — than in the mouse one, but have fewer connections in the hippocampus. Jonas says that this kind of information can be gleaned only from living tissue.

In a 2025 Cell study examining tissue taken from the hippocampus and cortex, his team also found that the electrical signals transmitted between neurons were more reliable and precise than they were in mouse brains5. The synapses in human brains successfully triggered the receiving cell to fire 90% of the time, compared with a 62% success rate in mice. Computer modelling by Jonas’s team suggests that reliable transmission could set the human brain apart from those of other species. “We are at the beginning of understanding this,” notes Jonas.

Meanwhile, Palmer has observed that the excitability of brain cells differs between humans and rodents6, which could be because human dendrites are twice as wide as those of mice. Differences in size also affect how the cells handle information, she says. Larger neurons with longer, bushier branches can form widespread networks, whereas smaller neurons restrict a network to their close neighbours.

Palmer also finds human tissue invaluable for studying disease. Cancers in mouse brains are generally composed of a limited number of cell types, whereas every single cell in a human brain tumour is different. Furthermore, most brain cancer research in mice has focused on one particular type of cancer, called glioblastoma.

According to recent reports, neurons from the human cortex next to their neighbours. Scientists can record from several branches of these complex neurons to monitor their activity.Credit: Jake Watson, Jonas group, ISTA.

Using slices of human brain tissue, Palmer and her team have found that cancer cells taken from aggressive tumours were more active than those in slower growing tumours7, boosting signalling and forming more synapses with neurons. The researchers also found that neurons were generally more active in people with aggressive tumours and that this increased activity leads to greater spread of cancer cells, confirming results from animal models.

In a study testing the efficacy of a drug for brain cancer, Palmer’s team also saw changes to excitability and signalling in neurons8. Together, the findings could explain how the drug slows down tumour growth, or halts it entirely.

One of the biggest challenges of working with living human brain tissue is a specialist technique that scientists need to learn. Called patch-clamping, the technique involves pressing the tip of a glass micropipette against the membrane surrounding a neuron and using suction to make a tight seal. A cell’s electrical activity can then be measured through one or several ion channels in the membrane. These measurements are used to study how a neuron behaves in response to different stimuli.

Patch-clamping was invented in the 1970s and is an indispensable tool in electrophysiology. It stands in stark contrast to techniques such as calcium imaging and optical imaging, which allow scientists to measure electrical activity in thousands of neurons at once. These techniques are more expensive but less technically challenging, indicates Palmer. In comparison, “patch-clamping takes a year to learn and years to understand,” she says. “You never master it.”.

Real Madrid news: Aurelien Tchouameni signs bumper upcoming Los Blancos contract with decade milestone in sight

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 13:37, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 13:38.
  • Real Madrid have announced that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.
  • The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 13:37, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 13:38.

Real Madrid have announced that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.

The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.

Following the final international break of the calendar year, Real Madrid return to action at the Bernabeu on Saturday afternoon, when top-flight regulars Celta Vigo are the visitors in La Liga.

The makeup of Los Blancos' squad has shifted massively over the past few years as a number of fresh attacking stars have arrived, including French superstar Kylian Mbappe and England's Jude Bellingham.

With his influence waning, Vinicius Junior has endured a difficult start to the current campaign, with the Brazil international struggling since Real Madrid waved goodbye to German legend Toni Kroos.

Communicating to supporters worldwide on their official website, Real Madrid confirmed some exciting news involving Tchouameni, who has started seven La Liga matches so far in the 2026-27 term.

Los Blancos have announced that the 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a bumper contract extension at the Bernabeu, committing his long-term future to the 15-time European champions.

Tchouameni's deal with Real Madrid now expires in June 2032, meaning that the Frenchman could spend a decade at the Spanish giants if he sees out at the length of his recently-agreed terms.

The midfielder joined from Ligue 1 outfit Monaco in the summer of 2022 on a deal running until June 2028, meaning that he was approaching the conclusion of his initial agreement at the club.

Tchouameni started the La Liga victories over Barcelona (2-1), Racing Santander (3-0) and Valencia (3-0) prior to the November international break and should play once again versus Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Racking up over 200 competitive appearances since his 2022 arrival from France, Tchouameni has become part of the furniture at Real Madrid, who are looking to repeat their former glories.

The departure of legendary German Kroos left a massive hole to fill in the middle of the park, and Los Blancos are focused on bringing through the next generation of club heroes under head coach Mourinho.

  • The 54-year-old Argentine arrives at the Theatre of Dreams with the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight games of 2026-27.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:04.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has reportedly prepared to enter talks over the Old Trafford future of Bruno Fernandes.

The 54-year-old Argentine arrives at the Theatre of Dreams with the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight games of 2026-27.

That woeful run was eventually enough to remove Michael Carrick from his post at Man Utd, with the club's hierarchy moving swiftly to lure Pochettino away from his duties with the United States on the international scene.

As well as Carrick, wonderkid JJ Gabriel has also departed the Red Devils this month, with the teenage sensation set to sign for European giants Real Madrid despite failing to make a first-team appearance for United.

Looking to avoid an unthinkable relegation this season, Man Utd are plotting significant additions to the playing squad during the January transfer window, with a Greek striker supposedly catching the eye.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano via Football Transfers, newly introduced Manchester United head coach Pochettino is set to be immediately involved in major talks at the Theatre of Dreams.

The report states that the Red Devils and captain Fernandes have been locked in discussions over a contract extension for the past five months, with an agreement yet to be reached by the two parties.

The 32-year-old's current deal at Old Trafford expires in June 2027, meaning that the Portuguese playmaker would be able to depart on a free transfer at the conclusion of this season.

It is understood that Man Utd are aiming to avoid that scenario, and now incoming boss Pochettino is set to join talks with the player and the club over the future of the influential attacker.

Fernandes supposedly retains interest from clubs in Italy, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, with Champions League-competing Galatasaray attempting to bring the former Sporting Lisbon man to Istanbul over the summer.

Whilst Manchester United's transfer activity since the exit of Sir Alex Ferguson has come under deserved criticism, there is no doubt that the signing of Fernandes was an excellent move by the fallen English powerhouses.

The 32-year-old has been an almost ever-present in the Red Devils ranks since joining from the Primeira Liga in January 2020, scoring 113 goals across a total of 341 competitive appearances.

Fernandes broke the Premier League assist record last season despite his side's immense struggles, and that theme of shining amid the chaos extends throughout the attacker's time in England.

By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026.

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson.

Devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor noted.

'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'.

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

Industry observers note that the freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Sources indicate that wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

According to recent reports, elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

Meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's looks suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

Industry observers note that melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

Sources indicate that the French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

According to recent reports, chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

According to recent reports, malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor noted: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’.

It has been revealed that A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor noted: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’.

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’.

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front.

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

According to recent reports, the Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

In the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz noted at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’.

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal.

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor stated: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’.

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz said: ‘They managed to score on their massive chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’.

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the fresh WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 14:12.
  • Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.
  • The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 14:12.

Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.

Palace have spent 14 consecutive seasons in the Premier League, and the capital club's board have taken drastic action to ensure that number becomes 15 at the end of the current campaign.

The Selhurst Park outfit entered the November international break in dire straits after a 3-1 loss to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, marking their fourth consecutive top-flight defeat following setbacks against rivals Brighton & Hove Albion, Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Particularly striking during that run were their struggles in front of goal and defensive frailties, highlighted by an alarming 12-1 aggregate score across those defeats that ultimately cost Sage his job.

Frank's reputation suffered during his spell as Spurs boss last season, but his previous work at Brentford should give the Selhurst Park faithful confidence that a turnaround is possible.

Nonetheless, it remains to be seen whether the Dane has conveyed his ideas in less than a week of training, with the international break also denying him access to his full squad, as the London club seek to end their four-match losing sequence.

A first victory since October and third overall would lift them above this weekend's 17th-placed hosts and potentially out of the bottom three, although the latter outcome depends on results elsewhere.

Coventry's 3-1 defeat at Everton before the pause left Frank Lampard's men alongside Arsenal and Manchester City as the only clubs yet to draw in this season's Premier League campaign.

However, while the defending champions and Man City occupy positions in the top three, Coventry's nine points leave them just one clear of the relegation places heading into a busy period.

Lampard's men can take encouragement from collecting six of those points in front of their adoring supporters, who witnessed October victories of 4-1 over Newcastle and 3-1 against Sunderland either side of a narrow 1-0 defeat to Fulham.

Although the absence of home clean sheets remains concerning, the Sky Blues' seven goals across their last three matches at the Coventry Building Society Arena represent clear progress after they failed to score in opening defeats to Hull City (1-0) and Brighton (5-0).

Now, the West Midlands side aim to secure consecutive home Premier League victories to avoid slipping into the bottom three.

Coventry City Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace form (all competitions):.

Caleb Yirenkyi and Bobby Thomas (calf) are doubtful for Coventry this weekend, while Luke Woolfenden (knee) and Josh Eccles (ankle) face late fitness tests; however, Frank Onyeka, Aurele Amenda (calf), Haji Wright (thigh) and Ephron Mason-Clark (knee) are expected to miss out.

Jack Rudoni is the only home player to have scored more than once, with the attacking midfielder's three goals accounting for 30% of the Sky Blues' tally of 10 this term.

After registering assists in consecutive appearances against Newcastle and Spurs in October, Brandon Thomas-Asante has dropped to the bench, but the Ghanaian forward will hope to play a pivotal role for Lampard's team this weekend.

One Palace player denied the opportunity to make an immediate impression is Jean-Philippe Mateta, who serves the second game of a three-match suspension following his straight red card in October's 2-0 defeat at Spurs.

Further concerns surround Ismaila Sarr (groin) and Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle), who are doubtful for this weekend's encounter and could leave Frank without several match-winners.

While former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) is also touch-and-go for Saturday's match, Chadi Riad's knee injury will keep him sidelined until 2027.

Coventry City possible starting lineup:.

Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Mfuni, Pinnock, Dasilva; Torp, Grimes; Sakamoto, Rudoni, Gboho; Awoniyi.

Crystal Palace possible starting lineup:.

Henderson; Richards, Disasi, Lerma; Mingueza, Wharton, Timber, Mitchell; Kamada, Pino; Nketiah.

Frank's appointment should provide Palace with renewed purpose, but Mateta's suspension and doubts over Sarr and Strand Larsen leave the visitors short of attacking options.

Coventry have scored seven goals across their last three home matches and could exploit the Eagles' defensive uncertainty to spoil the Dane's first assignment.

New US Congress should ‘reimagine’ science — not just return to the past

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The results of the US midterm elections will bring changes in Congress that could affect how science is governed.Credit: Aaron E.
  • The US Democratic Party’s sweeping victory, which saw the party take electoral majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, has rekindled optimism in the science community over the future of the nation’s research system.
  • ‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The results of the US midterm elections will bring changes in Congress that could affect how science is governed.Credit: Aaron E. Martinez/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty.

The US Democratic Party’s sweeping victory, which saw the party take electoral majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, has rekindled optimism in the science community over the future of the nation’s research system.

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science.

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science.

Science advocacy organizations and members of Congress are now rushing to address scientists’ most pressing question: how much money will be allocated to research in the spending bill for the fiscal year 2027?

According to recent reports, when it convenes on 3 January, the 120th Congress should also address two thornier, longer-term questions: who should get to participate in making decisions about science and technology? And how can policy institutions adapt to include more public voices?

According to recent reports, these questions sit at the centre of science’s ‘social contract’, the government-led support system that exchanges taxpayer funding and scientific autonomy for the promise of downstream public benefit. And they speak to a much older problem than the Second World War-era debates that created the modern US research system: the challenges of how to govern and the role of experts in democracies.

In the main, postwar US science policy has privileged experts over the public. In the 80 years since the publication of science adviser Vannevar Bush’s report Science, The Endless Frontier, the government has tested policy mechanisms that more closely align science with the nation’s social and economic needs. But public engagement remains in the wings.

Entire NSF science advisory board fired by Trump administration.

Entire NSF science advisory board fired by Trump administration.

It has been revealed that the National Science Foundation (NSF), a major funder of basic science at universities, has grown to embody the US social contract. And it has become a battleground for the competing visions of academia and the White House over federal science policy.

With no Senate-confirmed director and its acting director due to leave at the end of the year, the NSF faces a widening leadership gap. The American Institute of Physics and others have reported in detail on the firing, in April, of the National Science Board, which helps to oversee the NSF. Agency observers say that the absence of a Senate-confirmed director has made the NSF subject to greater White House direction.

The agency awarded nearly 50% fewer grants in the 2026 fiscal year than in the years from 2021 to 2024. The NSF has remarked that it has carried over more than $1 billion into the 2027 fiscal year to invest in agency priorities aligned with broader initiatives of the administration of President Donald Trump. It has two years to spend its research appropriations, although it does not typically carry over such a large share of its annual budget.

Over the past two years, the Trump administration has overhauled the nation’s long-standing social contract with science and, with it, the trusted partnership between universities and the federal government. The resulting impact on US science and increasing public attention on science policy has opened a unique window for reform. Congress should seize this opportunity to reimagine the nation’s science-policy institutions, rather than just trying to stitch them back together.

Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Industry observers note that luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

In a recent development, but here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

According to recent reports, croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Recent findings suggest that their newly introduced head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

Recent findings suggest that these could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Sources indicate that where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

The goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

Sources indicate that jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

Sources indicate that uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

Recent findings suggest that however, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Recent findings suggest that slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Sources indicate that thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

Reading will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Bromley to the Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are rock bottom in 24th.

Reading will be looking for an immediate response after suffering a 3-1 defeat to fellow promotion contenders Stockport County last weekend.

Jack Marriott equalised for the Royals after Kyle Wootton had opened the scoring, but goals from Ethan Ennis and Jack Diamond ultimately earned an important victory for the Hatters.

That result saw Leam Richardson's side drop out of the playoff places, although they could return to the top six with a victory over Bromley if other results go their way.

Reading have now lost their last two league games, having also been beaten 2-0 by local rivals Oxford United, but they remain one of the most dangerous sides in the division.

The Royals have scored 26 goals in 15 league games so far, a number only eclipsed by four other teams, and the return of top scorer Marriott from injury has come as a welcome boost.

The veteran striker has scored in his last two games across all competitions and bagged a total of nine goals in 10 league games.

Bromley, meanwhile, have struggled to make the step up to League One and are bottom of the division with just nine points from 13 games.

The Ravens are without a win in their last 10 games across all competitions and upcoming manager Karl Robinson says they "need to evolve" and "stick together" if they are to stay up this season.

Bromley's trip to Reading will be Robinson's first league game in charge, following a 2-0 defeat to Rotherham United in the FA Cup and a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons in the EFL Trophy.

It is worth noting that Bromley have never beaten Reading in a competitive fixture, although they did draw 1-1 in the EFL Cup earlier this season before the Royals triumphed on penalties.

Reading will be able to welcome back Paudie O'Connor and Andy Rinomhota from suspension and they should come straight into the side.

Marriott is expected to lead the line, with support out wide from Kyreece Lisbie and Daniel Kyerewaa.

Victor Adeboyejo remains a doubt for Bromley after he suffered an injury in the warm-up ahead of the Rotherham game, meaning Michael Cheek is likely to start up front against Reading.

Jodi Jones and Mickel Miller are set to continue out wide, with George Saville and Kamil Conteh starting in midfield.

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, O'Connor, Knight, Roberts; Wing, Rinomhota; Lisbie, Savage, Kyerewaa; Marriott.

George; Ifill, Grant, Taylor, Mendy; Saville, Conteh; Jones, McKiernan, Miller, Cheek.

Nelson Dida believes that Ruben Amorim is showing he is a ‘great’ coach, and he gave his take on the Endrick to AC Milan rumours.

If anyone knows about the pressure of playing for Milan, it is Dida. Having been at the club from 2000 to 2010, he made over 300 official appearances for the Rossoneri and was part of an era that brought in eight major trophies under Carlo Ancelotti.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He is widely regarded as one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation and was decisive in the 2003 Champions League final penalty shootout against Juventus. He also returned briefly as a goalkeeping coach, working for a year with Maignan.

Dida spoke to reporters who were present at the Galbiati Trophy and he answered a few questions regarding his former team, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

How do you think Amorim is doing?

“Amorim is proving to be a great coach. He took over Milan and is having a fantastic season. I think the attention is right because at Milan you can never make mistakes, but he has the ability to keep the team together to do well in the league.”.

If Maignan is hurt, would you come back and put the gloves on?

“We already have a goalkeeper at AC Milan: Lorenzo Torriani, a guy who’s doing well. I like him. Last year, too, he did well when he had opportunities. I think he’s a focused guy, if he gets more opportunities, he can continue to grow.”.

Are Milan growing towards something?

“Milan are slowly growing. They’re doing well in the league, I think we can still do more, while in Europe we’re still missing something.”.

Would Endrick be a good signing?

“Endrick is a great player for me. When I see him play, he looks a bit like Romario, who is a bit small, but when he’s in the penalty area, he’s decisive. When he’s had the opportunity to play, he’s also scored goals.

According to recent reports, “I think he can really do well for Real Madrid and the national team, but I don’t know if he’s available to join Milan. I hope a Brazilian returns to play in the Italian league soon and wears the Milan shirt.”.

#2275. Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1853 w)

Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.
  • A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.

A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.

Ferguson, who retired in 2013, won 38 major honours during a trophy-laden 26 years at Old Trafford.

And as the 84-year-old received plaudits across the footballing world, he enjoyed a celebratory intimate setting with some of his former players and actor James Nesbitt in Manchester.

Diehard United fan Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside Michael Carrick, Edwin van der Sar, Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea.

Recent findings suggest that but what are those former United players up to now? Daily Mail Sport takes a look...

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt (centre right) posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez.

Unless you've been on another planet, then you would know everything about Carrick this past week.

The 45-year-old was sacked as United head coach on Thursday morning after a disastrous start to the season.

Carrick, who has been replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, oversaw United's worst top-flight start since Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 Premier League matches as they sit 18th.

Furthermore this season, he only won three of 15 games in all competitions.

In a recent development, the downturn in the Red Devils' form is bewildering considering their upturn when Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January last season. He was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

Carrick was sacked as Manchester United head coach on Thursday morning by club chiefs.

He oversaw United's worst top-flight start in Premier League history with one win in 10 games.

Like Carrick, Evans is also out of a job having been part of his backroom staff at United as first-team coach.

After retiring as a player at the end of the 2024-25 season, Evans took up the position of head of loans and pathways at Carrington but left that role last December.

Following Amorim's sacking he returned to the club to help Fletcher during his caretaker manager stint before being kept on by Carrick.

Like Carrick, Evans was relieved of his United duties having been part of his backroom team.

The sole former player still connected directly with the club, Fletcher is their Under 18s head coach. The Scot had to pause his role last season when becoming the club's first-team interim head coach following Amorim's sacking in January - drawing 2-2 with Burnley in the Premier League before overseeing their FA Cup third-round home defeat by Brighton a few days later.

Having come through the club's academy, Fletcher knows what it takes to make the grade at the club and has the likes of Kai Rooney, son of Wayne, and Jacey Carrick, son of Michael, among his squad.

And Fletcher's young charges are enjoying a strong start to the season which has included six goals in wins over Liverpool (6-3) and Burnley (6-0) at the end of last month.

Fletcher is the Red Devils' U18s head coach - nurturing the club's latest crop of rising stars.

The former Red Devils captain had ambitions to go into coaching, having done his badges, but has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio - telling Gary Neville on The Overlap last July that he had put £4.5million into building 76 one or two-bedroom apartments in Belgrade, Serbia.

However, this summer it was reported that Vidic had been a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

According to Serbian media, encrypted messages show then-Serbia's football president Slavisa Kokeza wanted people to threaten Vidic after he had publicly criticised the Serbian Football Association (FSS) over the national side's failure to qualify for the Euro 2020 tournament.

In the reported devised plot in 2020, Kokeza reportedly told one contact to make it clear to Vidic that he should 'stay away from the association or he will end up in a ditch'.

As well as that, criminals were hired to monitor the former centre-back's movements in Milan, where he lived, and fit his car with a tracking device.

Following the revelations, Vidic and his legal team filed a criminal complaint and sought an investigation into the claimed plot.

'In mid-May, OCCRP and KRIK visited my home and told me they had obtained encrypted messages from Sky ECC (a now-defunct communication encryption service which EUROPOL said was widely used by criminals and was broken into by European police in 2021) and analysed them,' Vidic told The Athletic in July.

Recent findings suggest that 'The messages were said to have come from the then-president of the SFF in 2020. They were about me and how to stop me from talking to the media. At the time, I was commentating on the situation in Serbian football. I was living in Milan, Italy, where I stayed after finishing my career with Inter. I hadn't yet moved back to Serbia, where I am from and where I live.'.

Vidic, who has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio, was reportedly a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

Van der Sar's calm persona on the football pitch translated well into the boardroom during his near-seven-year stint at Ajax as their chief executive officer.

The former Manchester United goalkeeper joined the Dutch giants' board in 2012, becoming CEO in 2016. During his spell Ajax reached the 2017 Europa League final and 2019 Champions League semi-finals with a young exciting core of players including the likes of Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt.

The year Van der Sar left though Ajax finished third that season to qualify for the Europa League play-offs, missing out on the Champions League for the first time since 2009.

A few weeks later in July 2023, Van der Sar was put in intensive care after suffering a brain haemorrhage while on holiday in Croatia.

Three years on since recovering, Van der Sar is enjoying being away from football for the time being telling The Overlap in February: 'Now it's almost three years ago, so I've had time to recover with no stress, no phone in my hand - just doing the stuff that I've wanted to do.

'Wake up when you want, walk the dog, go swim in the sea, go on holiday. I went to New Zealand for two months with [wife] Annemarie - nice things that I never had the chance to do before.

'I started playing at 18 or 19, finished at 40, and at 41 I became one of the directors at Ajax until 53, so I thought it was the right time to take a step back. That's taken a little bit longer than I originally thought, to be fair, but we are enjoying ourselves very much.'.

Van der Sar was Ajax CEO for seven years before stepping down from the role in 2023.

The ex-goalkeeper is now enjoying life with wife Annemarie after a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

Like Carrick, Van Persie has turned his hand to first-team management since retiring.

Sources indicate that his first role was with Dutch outfit Heerenveen - signing a two-year contract with the club ahead of the 2024-25 season. However, his time there lasted just nine months as he took over the reins at Dutch giants Feyenoord.

However, his time in Rotterdam lasted just 16 months there when he was sacked in June. He had guided them to second in the Eredivisie but they finished 19 points behind champions PSV Eindhoven.

In explaining his sacking, newly-appointed technical director Devy Rigaux cited the style of play as a factor.

It has been revealed that 'We conducted a thorough internal analysis,' he said. 'In this, we took into account, among other things, the development of the style of play and the declining trend in terms of points total, both in Europe and in the Eredivisie.

'The conclusion was that it is better to start the next season with a upcoming head coach.'.

The 43-year-old is awaiting a fresh job, like Carrick.

Van Persie is right now without a managerial job after being sacked by Feyenoord in June.

The sole player from this list to still be playing, Hernandez made history by becoming the first-ever player signed to USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas.

In July, the 38-year-old penned a two-year deal with an option for a third year at the expansion club which will play in the second-tier of US football, below Major League Soccer.

The Mexican striker still has a few months to wait for his debut though, with the season not beginning until March 2027.

In the meantime, he was part of the FOX broadcast team for the recent World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, serving as an analyst.

Last year, Hernandez was caught up in a sexism storm, which he later apologised for, after he made a series of statements on TikTok 'promoting sexist stereotypes that are considered media violence and go against gender equality in sport'.

Hernandez remarked women are 'failing' and 'eradicating masculinity'.

'Don't be afraid to be women, to allow yourselves to be led by a man,' mentioned the former Mexico captain on social media.

His remarks sparked a backlash, which led to his apology which included him saying: 'I deeply regret any confusion or discomfort that my recent words have caused.'.

Hernandez was fined and warned about his future conduct.

Hernandez, who attended United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, is the only player still playing and has signed for USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas ahead of their fresh term.

Like the majority of the names here, O'Shea's post-playing career has seen him turn to coaching with his current role being the Republic of Ireland assistant head coach.

The 45-year-old has been in this position since August 2024, staying on with his homeland's setup following the appointment of Heimir Hallgrimsson as manager.

Industry observers note that O'Shea took charge of the team for four friendly fixtures that year following Stephen Kenny's departure in November 2023. His record read one win, one draw and two defeats in that period.

The former defender will be hoping to help his country qualify for Euro 2028 which will be played on home soil across the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales.

O'Shea is Republic of Ireland assistant head coach - a role he has held since August 2024.

Barcelona have reportedly earmarked Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and two other defenders as transfer targets ahead of the January window.

Hansi Flick's men have enjoyed an excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign on the domestic scene, winning 11 of their opening 12 top-flight contests, meaning that they sit top of the La Liga standings.

Barca have been linked heavily to new defensive additions in recent times, including Tottenham Hotspur man Pedro Perro, however, it is believed that the Catalans are not pursuing a deal for the World Cup winner in the New Year.

Head coach Flick is supposedly targeting the signing of a centre-back and a full-back during the upcoming trading point, aiming to strengthen his side's chances of winning the Champions League for the first time since 2015.

Hoping to record four consecutive competitive victories, Barcelona welcome Europe-chasing Villarreal to Camp Nou on Sunday afternoon, when club action will return following the international break.

As per Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barcelona will press forward in their search for a new defender during the January transfer window, in which head coach Flick is expected to be backed by sporting director Deco.

The report claims that Barca are keen on the cost-effective option of bringing Manchester United centre-back Martinez to the club, with the 2022 World Cup winner approaching the end of his contract at Old Trafford.

As well as the outspoken United star, it is understood that the La Liga leaders are also eyeing up a move for Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck, who is capable of playing at centre-back and left-back.

The 26-year-old was given his senior Germany debut by Barca boss Flick in March 2022, and the Dortmund sweetheart is supposedly available for £50m ahead of the winter transfer window.

Finally, it is believed that Barca's hierarchy are yet to shelve the possibility of signing Inter Milan and Italy defender Alessandro Bastoni, who is remarked to be open to a La Liga switch amid a £33m valuation.

After his explosive comments following defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, Martinez created a major rift between himself and the Manchester United board, as well as former head coach Carrick.

The general consensus is that the 28-year-old's time at Old Trafford is up, and it would be surprising if the Red Devils triggered the extension clause in the defender's current contract.

That being said, the arrival of compatriot Mauricio Pochettino could hand Martinez a second chance this season, with the centre-back potentially playing himself back into favour at the Theatre of Dreams.
